title: Search and Filter a Dataset
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of search and filter a dataset.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: Searching finds records that match a criterion; filtering returns a subset that meets one or more conditions. A project should define what is searchable, how comparisons work, whether matching is case-sensitive, and how empty results are handled. For larger datasets, efficiency may matter, but clear and correct behavior comes first.
understand.whyItMatters: Search and filter operations are common in apps and strengthen iteration, conditions, collections, and data handling.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
Searching finds records that match a criterion; filtering returns a subset that meets one or more conditions. A project should define what is searchable, how comparisons work, whether matching is case-sensitive, and how empty results are handled. For larger datasets, efficiency may matter, but clear and correct behavior comes first.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Use a small dataset of fictional records. Implement search by name and filter by category or numeric range. Define case handling and display a no-results message.
steps: Use a small dataset of fictional records. Implement search by name and filter by category or numeric range. Define case handling and display a no-results message.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Build a search/filter feature with two or more criteria, clear/reset behavior, empty-state handling, and tests for exact, partial, case-insensitive, and no-match results.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
Build a search/filter feature with two or more criteria, clear/reset behavior, empty-state handling, and tests for exact, partial, case-insensitive, and no-match results.
